the joint management policy could be used as a tool for forest conservation and poverty alleviation, provided that some conditions are met, which are: (i) the share of income generated from the secondary products going to local communities should at least be equivalent to that generated from timber exploitation; (ii) the marginal revenue from the exploitation of timber resources should be relatively higher to that from secondary activities; and (iii) external financing is required to secure local communities' cooperation for forest conservation.
